premise.coldViewerWhyCare: A familiar but puzzling change in the sense of passing time, explained with human evidence.
premise.viewerQuestion: Why can THC make time feel slower?
premise.earlyPayoff: The clock keeps ticking normally while our estimates of elapsed time may change.

beats.narration: Why can five minutes feel like forever after THC?
beats.visualPurpose: Show perceived slowness without claiming actual clocks change.
beats.visualAction: A large rendered clock resolves into two diverging rings within first three seconds.

beats.narration: The clock doesn't change. But your sense of time sometimes does.
beats.visualPurpose: Answer immediately: perception is distinct from actual elapsed time.
beats.visualAction: Keep the outer ring constant while inner markers diverge; illustrative, not measured values.

beats.narration: Your brain estimates passing seconds even when you're not watching a clock.
beats.visualPurpose: Explain everyday interval timing without asserting a single anatomical clock.
beats.visualAction: Visualize evenly spaced pulses feeding an abstract neural silhouette.

beats.narration: In controlled experiments with forty-four people, THC changed estimates of short time intervals.
beats.visualPurpose: Explain verified sample size and experimental seconds-range task.
beats.visualAction: Show anonymous THC and placebo columns without invented numeric outcome bars.

beats.narration: People who rarely used cannabis sometimes judged those intervals as longer than they were.
beats.visualPurpose: Describe the key response among infrequent users without claiming universal effects.
beats.visualAction: Extend a conceptual felt-time arc beyond the real-time arc, without fabricated scales.

beats.narration: Frequent users in that study did not show the same changes. Other studies have mixed results.
beats.visualPurpose: Avoid a single universal mechanism; acknowledge mixed study methods and findings.
beats.visualAction: Split cohorts and dissolve an overconfident certainty arrow into variable estimates.

beats.narration: So that slow-motion feeling? It's perception, not a broken clock. Follow for evidence, not hype.
beats.visualPurpose: Resolve the opening question and close with THS identity.
beats.visualAction: Reconcile the two rings and form a custom dark-organic THS cellular identity lockup.

beats.visualPurpose: Provide visible primary source after the explanation.
beats.visualAction: Quiet, high-contrast PMID source card; no spoken captions.
